definition: Embargo is an official government ban on trade or the movement of goods with a particular country or in a particular product.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word embargo. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know embargo should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After the missile tests, several countries placed an embargo on electronics exports to the regime.
A restriction limits some trade, while an embargo bans it outright by official government order.
An embargo cuts off trade on paper, while a blockade physically stops the ships and trucks from getting through at all.

A ban is an official rule forbidding something, and any authority can issue one — a school bans phones. An embargo is a particular kind of ban: a government's official halt to trade or the movement of goods, aimed at a country or a product. Every embargo is a ban; only banned commerce is an embargo.

A prohibition is a formal order forbidding an activity, whatever the activity is — parking, hunting, burning. An embargo is the trade-specific version: an official government ban on commerce or the movement of goods, usually aimed at another country. Call any forbidding a prohibition; reserve embargo for trade stopped by government order.

formal, news and policy register
Embargo appears constantly in news and policy writing, almost always with the verbs impose, enforce, or lift, and with the preposition on: a nation imposes an embargo on oil exports.
It names an official act by a government, never a personal refusal to buy something.
